module.name: output_impl
module.spec: Package cli/output/ contains: result.go (Result types), presenter.go (Presenter interface + Render), plain.go (PlainPresenter + format helpers), color.go (ColorPresenter), json.go (JSONPresenter), tty.go (IsTerminal + SelectPresenter + resolveTheme), theme.go (Theme struct + Style + DefaultTheme + AllElementIDs), themes.go (12 built-in themes), theme_load.go (LoadCustomTheme), user_settings.go (LoadUserSettings + SaveUserSettings), tokenize.go (syntax tokenizer), build.go (BuildListResult + BuildShowResult + EntityExists + edge predicates). Subpackage cli/commands/ contains one file per command plus command.go (interface + types), helpers.go (shared init/gitignore helpers), and friction.go (rate-limit telemetry). cli/registry.go has the Registry. cli/cli.go retains Run + RunWithRender + stripGlobalFlags. Every file in this layout is drift-tracked (see self_hosting_preserved).

Presenter interface in cli/output/presenter.go declares one method per Result type: Todo, List, Show, DiffClosure, DiffAll, Ok, Error, Text, Version. Three implementations (PlainPresenter, ColorPresenter, JSONPresenter) — one per output mode — each implement all methods. The Render(Presenter, Result) function dispatches a Result to the matching method via a single type-switch. See command interface.

Result types in cli/output/result.go. Sealed interface (unexported isResult method). Concrete types: TodoResult{State}, ListResult{State,Verbose,SpecContents,MarkerContents}, ShowResult{IsSpec,ID,Nodes,Edges}, DiffClosureResult{Hash,Diffs}, DiffAllResult{State,Closures}, ChangeSummaryResult{Summary,Preview,Message,Warning}, OkResult{Command,Message}, ErrorResult{Command,Message,Hint,Exit} (per the error result invariant), TextResult{Text}, VersionResult{Version}. ShowResult uses a closure-based shape (Nodes []ShowNode + Edges) from BuildShowResult's bidirectional BFS. ShowResult and ListResult carry pre-resolved content so presenters stay pure (no I/O). ChangeSummaryResult carries an optional Warning field for friction-bypass notices.
PlainPresenter in cli/output/plain.go. Methods are byte-identical migrations of the format* functions from the pre-refactor cli/cli.go. No I/O, no color, no JSON. See plain mode.

ColorPresenter in cli/output/color.go. Carries a Theme field selecting the active theme. Every method renders from Result data using theme element lookups (e.g. t.MarkerID.Apply(idString)) instead of hardcoded color helpers. The guardrail property is maintained because Style.Apply only wraps text in ANSI codes. colorizePatch applies per-line theme coloring (DiffAdd/DiffRemove/DiffHunk) to unified diff output. The Todo method formats closures: each closure shows hash, member counts, Events section (NODE-CHANGED/NODE-ADDED/NODE-REMOVED/EDGE-ADDED/EDGE-REMOVED/BROKEN-EDGE), Members section, and Inspect/Resolve commands using the closure hash. See color mode and theme system.

JSONPresenter in cli/output/json.go. Uses encoding/json with struct-driven field ordering and HTML escaping disabled for readability. Per-method serialization per the JSON schema. The marshal helper uses json.Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) and trims the trailing newline. Closure events carry a "kind" discriminator ("nodeChanged", "nodeAdded", "nodeRemoved", "edgeAdded", "edgeRemoved", "brokenEdge") so JSON consumers can dispatch on event kind. See JSON mode.

cli/commands/command.go defines Command interface (Run(ctx Context) (Result, int); Meta() Meta), Context struct (Args, Dir, Orch), Meta struct (Name, Short, Usage, Flags), and the Version package var. The Context carries the orchestrator so commands can call orch methods. Every command flows through the same uniform dispatch pipeline. Meta is the single source of truth for command metadata. See command interface and metadata single source.

cli/registry.go exports var Registry = map[string]commands.Command{...} mapping command names to Command instances. Commands needing embedded content (help text, skill guide, init template) receive it via struct fields set at Registry construction time. Provides derived helpers subcommandHelp(name) (returns cmd.Meta().Usage) and recognizedFlagsFor(cmd) (builds map from cmd.Meta().Flags). The rejectUnknownFlags function uses recognizedFlagsFor. See metadata single source.

The help text is currently still embedded as cli/help.txt (embedded via go:embed in cli.go). The HelpCommand returns it as a TextResult. In a future landing, the help text will be generated from the Registry (static prose from fragments.go + command table from Registry enumeration). See registry.
Spot-check tests assert stripANSI(ColorPresenter.X(r)) == PlainPresenter.X(r) for representative Result values, confirming the guardrail property holds for the closure-driven output shapes.

cli/output/theme.go defines Style{Color string; Bold bool; Dim bool} and Theme{Name string; MarkerID, SpecID, Filepath, LineNumber, Hash, StatusOK, StatusWarn, StatusError, SectionHeader, Command, Hint, DiffAdd, DiffRemove, DiffHunk, CodeComment, CodeString, CodeKeyword, CodeNumber Style}. Style.Apply(s string) string composes the ANSI SGR sequence: codes are collected in order — dim ("2"), bold ("1"), Color (raw SGR parameter) — joined by semicolons, wrapped as \x1b[CODESm + s + \x1b[0m. Zero-value Style (all fields empty/false) returns s unchanged — no escape codes emitted. Color accepts basic ("31"), bright ("91"), 256-color ("38;5;37"), and true color ("38;2;R;G;B") SGR parameters. The CodeXxx elements apply to syntax-highlighted code content (see code colorization). See theme system.

cli/output/themes.go exports 12 Theme vars and a map AllThemes = map[string]Theme{"default": DefaultTheme, "minimal": MinimalTheme, "monochrome": MonochromeTheme, "high-contrast": HighContrastTheme, "dark": DarkTheme, "light": LightTheme, "protanopia": ProtanopiaTheme, "solarized-dark": SolarizedDarkTheme, "solarized-light": SolarizedLightTheme, "gruvbox": GruvboxTheme, "nord": NordTheme, "dracula": DraculaTheme}. lookupTheme(name string) (Theme, bool) looks up by name (case-sensitive). Designer palette themes use 256-color SGR codes with attribution comments citing the original palette and its MIT license. See built-in themes.

cli/output/theme_load.go exports LoadCustomTheme(sess *fileio.Session) (Theme, error). Reads .drift/theme.xml via the Session. Parses <theme><element id="X" color="Y" bold="true|false" dim="true|false"/>...</theme> using encoding/xml. Requires all 18 element IDs present; returns an error naming the first missing element if any are absent. Returns (Theme{}, os.ErrNotExist) if the file does not exist — caller treats this as "no custom theme, use built-in". The returned Theme has Name="custom". See custom theme and fileio.Session.

cli/output/tokenize.go exports tokenizeLine(line string) []Token where Token{Type string; Text string} and Type is one of: "comment", "string", "keyword", "number", "plain". The tokenizer is a single-pass character scanner with states for string tracking (double-quote, single-quote, backtick) and comment detection (//, #, -- at word boundaries). Comment markers require preceding whitespace, start-of-line, or semicolon to avoid false positives on URLs and operators. The keyword set is a package-level map of ~80 common cross-language words (if, else, for, return, func, def, class, import, const, nil, true, false, etc.). Number detection matches digit sequences optionally containing a single dot. The tokenizer is language-agnostic by design — no file extension lookup, no per-language grammar. See code colorization and language agnostic.

cli/output/user_settings.go exports UserSettings{Theme string}, LoadUserSettings(sess *fileio.Session) (UserSettings, error), and SaveUserSettings(sess *fileio.Session, settings UserSettings) error. Reads/writes .drift/user-settings.xml via the Session in the format <settings><theme>NAME</theme></settings>. Returns (UserSettings{}, nil) if the file does not exist — this is the normal case for fresh projects. The file is NOT committed to git (listed in .drift/.gitignore, created by drift init). Created by `drift config theme NAME`. Consumed by resolveTheme during SelectPresenter (see theme resolution and fileio.Session).

PlainPresenter.Show renders the full citation closure of a single seed (spec or marker) as a stable text block. The header section prints the seed ID, kind, filepath, optional line range (markers only), hash, and a Deleted flag if the seed is gone from disk. A summary line gives node/edge/spec/marker counts and total content bytes. After the seed content, ancestors and descendants are rendered in separate sections (see output_impl.closure_classification) and markers in the closure get their own section. Edges are listed flat at the end as "From → To" lines. The whole block is right-trimmed of newlines before return. When the seed ID is not found in r.Nodes, Show returns a "<kind> <id> not found" string (the dispatch layer separately sets exit code 1 — see cli.show_command R6). Show consumes the pre-resolved ShowResult shape built by BuildShowResult; it does no I/O. See cli.show_command, output_impl.closure_classification, output_impl.section_rendering.

classifyClosureSpecs(r ShowResult, seedID) walks the closure's edges in both directions from the seed to partition reached specs into ancestors (specs that transitively cite the seed) and descendants (specs the seed transitively cites). It builds outgoing and incoming adjacency maps once, then BFS-walks outgoing from seedID to fixpoint for descendants and incoming from seedID to fixpoint for ancestors. The seed itself is excluded from both lists. Cycles in the spec graph are impossible (core.validate rejects directed cycles), so the BFS terminates at fixpoint without visited-set tricks beyond the per-walk membership check. Returned ancestors and descendants slices are sorted by ID for stable display. Markers in the closure are NOT classified here — they are leaf attendees (markers cannot be cited) and the Show method handles them in their own section. See output_impl.show_rendering.

renderSpecSection and renderMarkerSection are the per-node text renderers used by PlainPresenter.Show after the seed block. Each writes a header line (ID + filepath, with line range for markers), the node hash, an optional "Status: deleted from disk" line for deleted nodes, and — when content is present — a "--- content ---" separator followed by the raw content bytes and a trailing newline. The two functions are structurally identical except for the header line shape (specs have just filepath; markers have filepath:line-range). Both bail out early on a deleted node (no content section) and on an empty-content live node (no separator). They write into a shared *strings.Builder so the caller controls the surrounding context. See output_impl.show_rendering.

sortSpecsByID and sortMarkersByID are insertion-sort implementations that sort a slice of core.Spec / core.Marker in place by ID ascending. Insertion sort is chosen over sort.Slice because the typical spec/marker list is small (drift's own repo: ~180 specs and ~130 markers) and the comparison key is a cheap string compare. Both functions are used by PlainPresenter.List (and by extension ColorPresenter.List, which renders the same shape) so the specs and markers sections in `drift list` output are lexicographically ordered by ID — making the output diff-stable across runs even when the state store's slice order shifts. See cli.list_format, output_impl.edge_sort_helper.

sortEdgesByFromTo(edges) sorts a slice of core.Edge in place lexicographically by (From, then To) using an insertion sort. Used by PlainPresenter.List (and ColorPresenter.List) to render the Edges section in `drift list` output in a stable order. The state store does not guarantee any particular edge slice order across saves (the gob packfile round-trip can reorder), so without an explicit sort the Edges section would shuffle between runs, breaking diff-stable review. The same O(n²) insertion-sort rationale applies as output_impl.list_sort_helpers: drift's own repo has ~290 edges and the comparison key is two cheap string compares. See cli.list_format, output_impl.list_sort_helpers.

isSpecID(id) reports whether a string carries the module-qualified shape (contains at least one dot). It is implemented via containsDot(s), a single-pass byte scan that returns true on the first '.'. The dot-presence check is intentionally looser than the orchestrator's isSpecID (which requires exactly one dot) — output-side dispatch uses it only to pick a lookup branch (specs vs markers) in BuildShowResult and EntityExists, where any dotted ID is presumed to be a spec. Misses fall through to the marker lookup, which is exhaustive; a malformed ID simply reports "not found" via the standard path. The two functions live in cli/output/build.go alongside the dispatch helpers that consume them. See cli.show_command.

Overview: The coverage command's output flows through the same presenter pipeline as every other command (PlainPresenter / ColorPresenter / JSONPresenter). The new result type, CoverageResult, carries the fully-resolved coverage data so presenters stay pure (no I/O, no recomputation).
Defined terms: CoverageResult — the Result type returned by CoverageCommand.Run and consumed by all three presenters FileCoverage — per-file shape: {Filepath, TotalLines, CoveredLines, Percent, LinkedSpecCount} DirectoryCoverage — per-directory shape used in --by-file mode: {Directory, TotalLines, CoveredLines, Percent, LinkedSpecCount} CoverageSummary — header block: {FilesScanned, TotalLines, CoveredLines, Percent, UnlinkedMarkers []string, OrphanSpecs []string, ThresholdValue int (0 = unset), ThresholdPassed bool}
Requirements: R1. CoverageResult MUST be added to the Result sealed interface (unexported isResult method on each concrete type — see output_impl.result_types). The Render type-switch in presenter.go MUST dispatch CoverageResult to a new Coverage method on each Presenter. R2. CoverageResult MUST carry the active "mode" (per-file vs per-directory) so presenters render the right table shape without re-deriving it. Field name: Mode string with values "file" or "directory". R3. CoverageResult MUST carry FileRows []FileCoverage in mode "file" and DirectoryRows []DirectoryCoverage in mode "directory". Exactly one of the two is non-empty per result (the unused field is nil). R4. CoverageResult MUST carry a CoverageSummary value with the header numbers, the unlinked-marker IDs, the orphan-spec IDs, and the threshold gate state. The threshold field uses 0 to mean "unset" (since 0 is not a useful threshold value in practice — coverage is never gated at exactly 0%). R5. PlainPresenter.Coverage MUST render the per-file table in the format documented in cli.coverage_command R5: aligned columns "filepath | N lines | M covered (P%) | K specs", sorted by gap desc then filepath asc. The directory table (--by-file mode) uses the same column shape with directory in place of filepath. R6. PlainPresenter.Coverage MUST right-align numeric columns and left-align filepath/directory. Percent is rendered with no decimal places (whole percent). R7. ColorPresenter.Coverage MUST produce byte-identical output to PlainPresenter.Coverage after stripping ANSI codes (the guardrail property — see output.guardrail_property). Color is applied via Theme elements: low coverage rows use StatusError, mid coverage use StatusWarn, high coverage use StatusOK. The threshold bands are theme-resolved, not hardcoded. R8. JSONPresenter.Coverage MUST emit a structured object with top-level fields: mode, summary (object matching CoverageSummary), rows (array of FileCoverage or DirectoryCoverage objects). The shape mirrors the existing list/todo JSON shapes for consumer consistency. Hashes are not included (coverage is a runtime computation, not a baseline view). R9. The BuildCoverageResult helper in cli/output/build.go (sibling to BuildListResult and BuildShowResult) MUST construct the CoverageResult from a scanner scan + baseline state, performing the line counting per cli.coverage_line_counting. The helper does I/O (reads files for line counting); the presenters do not. R10. CoverageResult MUST implement the Result interface (isResult method) so it flows through the existing Render(Presenter, Result) dispatcher without special-casing.
See also: cli.coverage_command, output_impl.result_types, output_impl.presenter_interface, output.guardrail_property, output.modes.
